questions.stem: The FIRST UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed from India (1983, along with Ajanta and Ellora caves) includes:
questions.explanation: India's first four UNESCO WHS were inscribed together in 1983: Agra Fort, Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Taj Mahal. Agra Fort is listed first alphabetically. Khajuraho (1986), Sun Temple Konark (1984) came slightly later.

questions.stem: Match the UNESCO WHS with its LOCATION. A. Hampi.  B. Khajuraho.  C. Mahabalipuram.  D. Konark. List-II: 1. Karnataka.  2. Madhya Pradesh.  3. Tamil Nadu.  4. Odisha.
questions.explanation: Hampi (Karnataka) — Vijayanagar ruins, 1986. Khajuraho (MP) — Chandela temples, 1986. Mahabalipuram (TN) — Pallava shore temple, 1984. Konark Sun Temple (Odisha) — 1984, Eastern Ganga dynasty.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a NATURAL (not cultural) UNESCO site in India?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam, 1985) is a natural WHS — one-horned rhino stronghold. Other natural WHS in India: Manas NP (Assam), Keoladeo (Rajasthan), Sundarbans (WB), Nanda Devi + Valley of Flowers (UK), Great Himalayan NP (HP), Western Ghats (cluster of 39 sites).

questions.stem: The 'MOUNTAIN RAILWAYS OF INDIA' UNESCO inscription covers which railway lines?

options.option_text: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, Nilgiri Mountain Railway, and Kalka-Shimla Railway
Konkan Railway and Palace on Wheels
All trains running in the Himalayan region

questions.explanation: Three narrow-gauge lines are bundled as 'Mountain Railways of India' WHS: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (inscribed 1999), Nilgiri Mountain Railway (added 2005), Kalka-Shimla Railway (added 2008).

questions.stem: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi — a UNESCO WHS — is architecturally significant because it:

options.option_text: Is the oldest mosque in India
Was the prototype inspiration for the Taj Mahal
Is made entirely of red sandstone without marble

questions.explanation: Built 1569-70 by Humayun's widow Bega Begum, architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas (Persian). First garden-tomb on the subcontinent; charbagh layout; central double dome. Directly influenced the Taj Mahal (1653). Inscribed 1993.

questions.stem: The WESTERN GHATS are recognised as a UNESCO WHS primarily for:

options.option_text: Their exceptional biodiversity and endemic species
Being the highest mountain range in Asia

questions.explanation: Inscribed 2012. Western Ghats (Sahyadri) run ~1,600 km along the west coast — a biodiversity hotspot with >7,400 flowering plants, 325 threatened species. Older than the Himalayas geologically. The inscription covers 39 component sites across Kerala, Karnataka, TN, Maharashtra.

questions.stem: Consider the following about the TAJ MAHAL. 1. Built by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died during childbirth in 1631. 2. Chief architect Ustad Ahmad Lahauri; took ~22 years to build (1632-1653). 3. Listed as a UNESCO WHS in 1983. 4. Declared one of the 'New Seven Wonders of the World' in a 2007 global poll. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. The white marble came from Makrana (Rajasthan), red sandstone from Fatehpur Sikri. The main workforce was ~20,000 craftsmen.
